reason: Gentle collisions should help the rocky grains stick together before gravity can gather larger bodies.

choice.combine: A mixture of stone and metal

expectation: The stone and metal grains will form larger aggregates.

effect: Gentle collisions made rocky pebbles, but further simple sticking faces bouncing and fragmentation.
reaction: The growth barrier makes the next stage more interesting.
reason: Gas drag may concentrate the pebbles rather than relying on further sticking.
expectation: Gas drag will help gather or move the rocky pebbles toward a denser swarm.

effect: Gas drag produced drifting rocky pebbles, which can concentrate in structured regions.
reaction: The distinction between drift and concentration is useful.
reason: A pressure maximum is a plausible place for drifting pebbles to accumulate.

choice.with: A pressure maximum in the disk

expectation: The pressure maximum will concentrate the rocky pebbles into a denser swarm.

effect: The pressure maximum concentrated the drifting pebbles into a dense rocky swarm, ready for gravity to act.
reaction: It's satisfying to see a route around the sticking barrier.
reason: Gravity within the dense swarm should bring its rocky solids together into planetesimals.

choice.combine: A dense swarm of rocky solids

expectation: The swarm will collapse into rocky planetesimals.

effect: Gravity collapsed the rocky swarm into planetesimals, completing the rocky goal; the icy goal remains.
reaction: The progression from drifting pebbles to gravitational collapse was satisfying.
reason: The icy material may begin growing through gentle collisions, as the rocky mixture did.

choice.combine: An outer-disk store of ice and dust

expectation: The ice and dust will form larger icy aggregates or pebbles.

effect: Gentle collisions produced icy pebbles containing rock and volatile material.
reaction: The parallel with rocky pebble formation is clear.
reason: Gas drag was consumed earlier, so I’ll check how the icy pebbles can progress.
expectation: The inspection will reveal an available route toward icy planetesimals.

effect: The inspection automatically concentrated the icy pebbles into a dense swarm at the pressure maximum.
reaction: I was surprised the icy route did not require a separate drag step.
reason: Gravity collapsed the rocky swarm into planetesimals, so it should do the same for the icy swarm.

choice.combine: A dense swarm of icy solids

expectation: The icy swarm will collapse into icy planetesimals.

effect: Gravity formed icy planetesimals and completed the remaining goal; they are possible water carriers, not the only source of terrestrial hydrogen.
reaction: The parallel collapse was satisfying, and the qualification about water sources was useful.

mostWorthwhile.text: Concentrating drifting pebbles and collapsing the swarm was most worthwhile: it showed how gravity can bypass the limits of simple sticking.

leastWorthwhile.text: The icy pebble stage was somewhat repetitive after the rocky sequence, though it established that the bodies contain both rock and volatile material.

surprise.text: Inspecting the icy pebbles automatically combined them with the pressure maximum; unlike the rocky route, it needed no separate drag action.

arbitrary.text: The different handling of gas drag felt a little arbitrary: it was consumed in the rocky route but described as acting in the icy route without a separate action.

continue.text: I would continue: the growth barrier and gravitational collapse made me curious about how these small bodies become worlds.
